spec.full_target:
# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
spec.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.

definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, using extended distance and sup(empty)=0. For bounded subsets of a Euclidean space it is identified with its finite nonnegative real value; diam(empty)=0.

definitions.type: scale contents H^s_delta(A) and unnormalized Hausdorff measure H^s(A), valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use

This is the unnormalized library Hausdorff measure, including the library extended-real-power convention at a=0. Its values on arbitrary sets are outer-measure values. No cover formula is assumed by this declaration; M001 supplies that formula.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive real exponent s.

argument.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

produces.statement: If 0<s<dim_H(A), H^s(A)=infinity; if dim_H(A)<s, H^s(A)=0; if H^s(A)=0, dim_H(A)≤s; if H^s(A)=infinity, dim_H(A)≥s.

argument.text: The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of N001.

locals.declaration: Choose b>0 with E⊆[-b,b]^n as supplied by F001.
Let h be an arbitrary mesh size, temporarily 0<h≤1.

argument.text: By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

produces.statement: There exists a positive real b with E⊆[-b,b]^n.

argument.text: Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n, D is finite, and n=0 implies E=R^0 and D=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves N002.

locals.declaration: For nonempty V_i set J_i=(inf(V_i)-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup(V_i)+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); set J_i=empty for empty V_i.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion.

produces.statement: dim_H(I)≤1, and for every real u>1, H^u(I)=0.

argument.text: Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of N003.

locals.declaration: Choose a countable r-cover W of E with total q-cost<epsilon/2, as asserted by F001.
For nonempty W_i of positive diameter set U_i=W_i. If W_i={x}, set U_i to the open Euclidean ball centered at that unique x with diameter beta_i (radius beta_i/2). For empty W_i set U_i=empty.
Set K={i∈N:U_i is nonempty}; use K as the index set after discarding empty members.
For i∈K set r_i(i)=diam(U_i), written r_i in formulas.
For i∈K set N_i(i)=ceil(1/r_i(i)), written N_i.

argument.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Push forward the interval covers that give H^a(I)=0 for a>1 in N003; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0 for all a>1. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a for every a>1 and hence dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1 and record F000.

For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. Such covers exist, for example by the finite-ball-cover assertion in N002. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

produces.statement: There exists a sequence W of subsets of R^n covering E, with diam(W_i)≤r for all i and sum_i diam(W_i)^q<epsilon/2.

argument.text: Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

produces.statement: The family (U_i)_(i∈K) covers E, 0<r_i≤r≤1 for i∈K, r_i=diam(U_i), and sum_(i∈K)r_i^q<epsilon.

argument.text:
For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.
A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

locals.declaration: Set μ=λ|I, Lebesgue measure restricted to I.

argument.text: Fix s>0, delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L1: V covers F and diam(V_i)≤delta for all i. Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

produces.statement: V covers F, rho_i≤delta, diam(A_i)≤rho_i, diam(B_i)≤rho_i, and c=H^s_delta(E)<infinity; nonempty B_i are bounded.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. This construction needs no measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i.

produces.statement: For every i, B_i⊆J_i, J_i is open and measurable, and |J_i∩I|≤|J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i.

argument.text: Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

produces.statement: Each f_i is nonnegative and Borel measurable; for every u∈I, c≤sum_i f_i(u).

argument.text:
Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
Here the middle equality is the integral of a measurable indicator times its nonnegative coefficient. The first inequality inside the sum uses F002 and distributivity of nonnegative sums. Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. Otherwise F004 holds for every epsilon>0 with c and V fixed, so letting epsilon decrease to zero gives the same inequality c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The cover V was arbitrary under L1. Take the infimum over all its possible delta-covers of F and discharge L1, obtaining H^s_delta(E)≤H^(s+1)_delta(F). Since s>0 and delta>0 were arbitrary, this is precisely N005.

applications.bindings: Set α=R, m=borel(R), μ=λ restricted to I, β=N, and f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t).
hypothesis_checks: D008 gives Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line; restriction to the Borel interval I is a measure on that same measurable space, as defined at S004.
The index type is N, which is countable.
F003, established in S003 from openness of J_i and constant nonnegative coefficients, proves Borel measurability of every f_i, hence almost-everywhere measurability for the restricted measure.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary positive lower bound T.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D>0 and L2: 0<s<D for arbitrary real s. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By its definition as the supremum of scale contents, for every T>0 there exists delta>0 with H^s_delta(E)>T. Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, because a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. Thus such lower bounds also hold at arbitrarily small scales. N005 applies at each such delta and gives H^(s+1)_delta(F)≥H^s_delta(E)>T. Its supremum is therefore infinite: H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dim_H(F)≥s+1. Record F001.

By N002, D is a finite real number; under L1 it is positive. F001 holds for every s with 0<s<D. Such s can increase to D, so their s+1 have supremum D+1 and dim_H(F)≥D+1. Equivalently any number below D+1 is below some s+1 with 0<s<D. Discharge L2 in this universal limiting argument, and then discharge L1 to obtain the full conditional statement N006.

locals.type: sequence of subsets of Euclidean R^(n+1)
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary sequence V, temporarily a delta-cover of F.

argument.text: Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

produces.statement: The restriction of f to I is an isometric embedding and f(I)⊆F.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). This proves the particular dimension-monotonicity implication used here directly from covers. N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity. N001 applied to F and exponent s yields dim_H(F)≥s.

Since F002 holds for every s with 0<s<1, letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)≥1. Discharge L2. Under L1, 1=D+1, so this proves the asserted bound. Discharge L1 to obtain N007. The argument used only the isometric embedding from a point of E, and applies unchanged to the singleton ambient space R^0.

N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×[0,1] and D=dim_H(E), with the Euclidean identification of D006, proves the complete target P.
